summary_paragraph: A 52-year-old female with systemic lupus erythematosus, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and a history of vascular disease was admitted for evaluation of progressive exertional chest pain and shortness of breath over the prior week. The pain was left-sided, worse when lying flat, and improved with sublingual nitroglycerin. She had no signs of acute myocardial infarction, with stable cardiac enzymes and no new ECG changes beyond baseline. A chest X-ray showed no acute process. Her symptoms improved during the hospital stay with medical management. Given her cardiovascular risk factors and persistent symptoms, she was started on isosorbide mononitrate for angina prophylaxis and referred for outpatient pharmacological stress echocardiography to evaluate for coronary artery disease. She remained stable, completed dialysis without complications, and was discharged home with follow-up arranged with cardiology and her primary team.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease with stage 5 chronic kidney disease or end stage renal disease
Glomerular disease in systemic lupus erythematosus
